hooks.text: Space Shuttle Atlantis lost over seven hundred thermal tiles in orbit.
How did Space Shuttle Atlantis survive reentry with over seven hundred missing tiles?
A missing heat shield tile saved Space Shuttle Atlantis from burning up entirely.

title: The Shuttle That Survived Seven Hundred Missing Tiles
description: Discover how Space Shuttle Atlantis survived a catastrophic tile loss during a classified 1988 mission.

beats.text: Space Shuttle Atlantis lost over seven hundred thermal tiles during flight.
beats.visual: Space Shuttle Atlantis in orbit during STS-27, 1988

beats.text: On December 2, 1988, ablative insulating material from the right solid rocket booster struck the orbiter.

queries: Space Shuttle solid rocket booster launch

beats.text: Eighty-five seconds into ascent, severe debris tore into the ship's vulnerable belly.

Orbiter heat shield cross section illustration

beats.text: Using the Canadarm, the crew inspected the heavy damage and grainy images were sent to Mission Control.
beats.visual: Space Shuttle Canadarm manipulator system in payload bay, 1988

beats.text: Engineers dismissed the footage as mere lights and shadows, leaving commander Robert Hoot Gibson convinced they would die.
Atlantis survived fiery reentry because a missing tile sat squarely over a thick aluminum antenna plate.
